data.title: How a sewage treatment plant works

sentences.text: If you pipe a town's toilets straight into a river, you have a sewer.
But the river turns dark brown and stinks.
So you fill a tank, where solids sink and scum floats.
But it catches only 45 to 65 of every 100 bits of waste, so the water stays dark.
So you add a tank and blow in air for bacteria.
This is a sewage treatment plant.
Bacteria eat the rest, and clear water flows to the river.
But now sludge piles up on the floor.
So you pump it to a digester, and its gas burns.
The average American sends about 82 gallons a day.
Add a fence and young trees around the plant.
Congratulations, you have built a sewage treatment plant.
